scenes.title: Table for two
scenes.summary: Order a meal, ask for changes, and pay.

turns.message: Hi there! Are you ready to order?
turns.hint: You need a bit more time.
wrongReplies: Can you give me one more minute time?
I need a minute more, please me.
turns.note: A polite, natural way to ask for more time.

turns.message: Sure, no rush. Any questions about the menu?
wrongReplies: What you recommend me?
Which food you advice?
turns.note: Ask for someone’s suggestion about what to order.

turns.message: The grilled salmon is really popular tonight.
wrongReplies: I will take the grilled salmon for me.
Give to me the grilled salmon.
turns.note: “I’ll have…” is a common way to order food.

turns.message: Great choice! It comes with a red onion salsa.
turns.reply: Could I get it without onions?
wrongReplies: Can you remove me the onions?
I want it no onions inside.
turns.note: A polite way to ask for an ingredient to be left out.

turns.message: How was everything? Can I get you anything else?
turns.reply: Could we get the check, please?
wrongReplies: Can we have the account paper?
Bring us the money thing.
turns.note: In the US, “the check” is the bill at a restaurant.

scenes.closing: Here you go. Thanks for coming in! 😊

scenes.title: Coffee run
scenes.summary: Order coffee and breakfast at a café.

turns.message: Morning! What can I get you?
turns.hint: A coffee you’ll take with you.
turns.reply: Can I get a coffee to go?
wrongReplies: Can I get a coffee for going?
Can I take coffee out to go away?
turns.note: “To go” means you will take the food or drink away.

turns.reply: Could you make that with oat milk?
wrongReplies: Can you put the oats milk on it?
Make it with milk from oats, can?
turns.note: Use “with” to say which milk or ingredient you want.

turns.message: Anything to eat? Our egg and cheese rolls just came out.
turns.hint: Eggs and cheese inside a roll.
wrongReplies: I’ll take a sandwich of breakfast.
I’ll buy bread with morning food.
turns.note: A breakfast sandwich usually has egg and other fillings in bread.

turns.message: How do you like your eggs?
wrongReplies: Scrambling, please.
In cooked pieces, please.

turns.message: Here you go! How’s the coffee?
wrongReplies: It has a big force!
It’s very powerful taste!
turns.note: “Pretty” can mean “fairly” or “quite” in casual speech.

scenes.closing: Haha, that’ll wake you up ☕ Have a good one!
